title: Symmetry-Constrained Cavity Block Optimization with Bilateral Coupling
scientific_hypothesis: Enforcing strict bilateral symmetry on the central cavity block (layers 6-14) will reduce the effective degrees of freedom while preserving the resonant transmission physics, enabling faster convergence to the true resonance optimum and eliminating the asymmetric thickness excursions observed in iteration_05.
design_principle: Fabry-Perot interferometer with symmetric defect cavity: outer DBR mirrors provide broadband reflection, central cavity layers create resonant transmission peak at 1550 nm. Symmetry constraint reduces optimization complexity while maintaining physical resonance conditions.
proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica (21 layers total: 5 outer mirror pairs + 1 cavity pair + 5 inner mirror pairs, with layers 6-14 constrained as symmetric conjugates)
design_variables: layers_6-10 thicknesses (cavity block, with layers_11-14 as symmetric conjugates)
manufacturing_considerations: symmetry constraint may simplify deposition monitoring
quarter-wave initial thicknesses provide fabrication-friendly starting point
theory_basis: Defective DBR bandpass filter theory: (HL)^N D(LH)^N structure creates transmission peak at defect resonance
Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda0/4 for DBR mirrors
Half-wave cavity optical thickness n*d = lambda0/2 for resonance
expected_advantages: Preserves resonance physics from successful iteration_05 design
known_risks: Symmetry constraint may prevent discovery of superior asymmetric solutions
May limit sideband suppression if asymmetry is physically beneficial
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 Fabry-Perot bandpass filter on Fused Silica substrate for 1550 nm LiDAR application. Layer sequence: Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5. Enforce strict bilateral symmetry constraint: layer_6 thickness = layer_14 thickness, layer_7 = layer_13, layer_8 = layer_12, layer_9 = layer_11, layer_10 is the center cavity layer (self-symmetric). Initialize outer mirror layers (0-5, 15-20) at quarter-wave thicknesses (Ta2O5: 184.5 nm, SiO2: 267.2 nm). Initialize cavity block layers (6-14) at 225 nm mean thickness. Optimization bounds: 50-450 nm for all layers. Perturbation amplitude: ±10 nm around initialization. Evaluate transmittance spectrum at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Score: maximize transmittance at 1550 nm (weight 1.0), minimize average transmittance in 1400-1500 nm band (weight 0.5), minimize average transmittance in 1600-1700 nm band (weight 0.5). Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Iteration_05 achieved 0.9745 score but showed asymmetric cavity thickness excursions. Feedback directive specifies enforcing bilateral symmetry on layers 6-14 to eliminate chaotic excursions and accelerate convergence to true resonance optimum.
